chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Safwan from Ibn Muskhan from Muhammad al-Halabi said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Nothing from the fish is disliked (makruh) except the Jari.

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him)
key_terms.الْجَرِيِّ: A specific type of fish, often identified as the sturgeon or a similar species, which is considered makruh (disliked but not forbidden)

ai.seo_question: Which type of fish is considered makruh in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the general permissibility of fish in Shia jurisprudence, identifying 'al-Jari' (often interpreted as the sturgeon or a specific scaly fish) as the sole exception. This ruling is foundational in distinguishing between fish with scales and those without, a key criterion in Shia fiqh for determining halal seafood.
